headline: Seven-country baseline health/school accessibility under the M3 road-quality model.
key_result: Baseline 60-min health access ranges from 35.91% in Ethiopia to 90.69% in the Philippines; school access ranges from 48.51% to 98.75%.

headline: Removing all unpaved arterial roads identifies dependence on unpaved roads.
key_result: Large losses in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, and Bangladesh; this is a stress test, not a realistic simultaneous-failure scenario.

headline: Surface-aware flood scenario per country.
key_result: Pakistan and Mozambique show the largest current-footprint losses; several other national footprints intersect few arterial roads.

headline: 18 real flood/cyclone footprints plus a DFO 1985-2010 event audit.
key_result: Pakistan health 60-min loss ranges from -0.785 to -9.690 pp across events; Mozambique ranges from -0.017 to -15.795 pp. Equal-event expectations are within-sample, not annual expectations.

headline: Parallel health and school accessibility outputs.
key_result: Health and school access differ systematically; Ethiopia has the largest health deficit, while Bangladesh school exposure is also substantial.

headline: Road class vs class+surface vs class+surface+width.
key_result: Ignoring surface/width overstates access: Mozambique baseline health M1 77.88% vs M3 72.86%; Pakistan M1 46.85% vs M3 43.95%.

headline: Planet predictions greatly reduce unknown surface share.
key_result: Pakistan known surface rises from OSM 30.7% to Planet 94.6%; Ethiopia from 34.6% to 91.9%. Planet changes downstream access most where OSM coverage is weak.

headline: Compare all-remove, all-slow, surface-aware, and surface-only disruption rules.
key_result: Mozambique health loss is -35.67 pp under all-remove, -9.01 under all-slow, and -15.80 under surface-aware; hazard-rule choice materially changes conclusions.

headline: Vary class speeds, surface multipliers, width multipliers, and flood deceleration.
key_result: Mozambique health baseline interval width is 8.67 pp; Pakistan hazard deceleration interval width is 6.43 pp.

headline: Snapping, hazard matching, MAUP, and last-mile sensitivity.
key_result: 0.05-degree aggregation lowers mean 60-min access by 24.26 pp and 0.10-degree by 36.00 pp; last-mile access lowers it by 9.20 pp.

headline: Weiss/Nelson 2015 city-access raster and UN SDG 9.1.1/RAI comparison.
key_result: Country mean travel-time correlations are strong (health Spearman 0.714; school 0.679), but threshold access correlations are weak because city access and service access differ.

headline: OSRM/Google/OpenRouteService comparison not yet configured.
key_result: Requires API keys or locally built routing networks with comparable origins and destinations.

headline: Mozambique 2026 audit, Cyclone Idai status validation, true-buffer rules, and Nepal 2026 Copernicus validation.
key_result: Idai direct flood recall is 11.38%, while flood5km OR unpaved reaches F1 0.758. Nepal 2026 direct observed-event overlap reaches precision 91.01%, recall 86.43%, and F1 0.887.

headline: Independent registry audits plus noded-network facility-corrected main-model reruns.
key_result: On noded networks, Ethiopia health rises from 52.45% OSM to 93.20% OSM+registry; Bangladesh school rises from 93.77% to 97.30%; Mozambique health rises from 75.53% to 84.35%.

headline: GHS-SMOD urban/rural access disparities at 1 km.
key_result: Kenya baseline health gap is 20.00 pp; Mozambique baseline school gap is 35.30 pp; hazard expands Mozambique health gap to 26.29 pp.

headline: GDL/World Bank analysis plus topology-corrected Mozambique SHDI rerun.
key_result: In noded Mozambique, SHDI-health correlation shifts from -0.509 to +0.390 and SHDI-school from +0.254 to +0.821; the urban disconnect artifact is resolved for Mozambique but not yet the other six countries.

headline: Gini and concentration indices for travel-time outcomes.
key_result: School travel-time Gini is especially high; flood-added travel is concentrated in lower-density cells in several countries.

headline: Population-weighted path-use intensity, road removal, and noded South Sofala restoration.
key_result: Arterial top 1% medical road removal causes 5-7 pp losses. On South Sofala noded network, restoring 10% by population dependency recovers +9.28 pp health and +4.60 pp school access.

headline: Post-flood restoration strategies.
key_result: Population-dependency ordering outperforms random and shortest-length ordering; Pakistan 10% restoration yields +3.03 pp health and +3.87 pp school access.

headline: Upgrade high-dependency or high-exposure unpaved roads, including noded South Sofala.
key_result: Paving gives larger resilience gains than routine gains. In noded South Sofala, 10% paving yields +3.68 pp hazard health access; hazard-exposure prioritisation dominates.

headline: Greedy road selection under length budgets, including noded South Sofala.
key_result: For flood resilience, hazard exposure per km dominates. In noded South Sofala, a 10% length budget yields +3.11 pp hazard health access; random yields only +0.86 pp.

headline: Joint sampling of class speed, surface, width, unknown allocation, and flood deceleration.
key_result: Pakistan school hazard interval width is 7.11 pp and Mozambique school width is 6.27 pp; population/facility uncertainty not yet sampled.

headline: Alternative assumptions for unknown surface roads.
key_result: Unknown handling matters most under hazard: unknown-as-unpaved causes up to -3.58 pp Mozambique health access relative to unknown-slow.

headline: Random/class deletion plus topology-noded Planet+OSM networks for all seven countries.
key_result: Noded networks raise baseline health access by 47.66 pp in Pakistan, 25.31 pp in Ethiopia, 23.25 pp in Kenya, 20.60 pp in Bangladesh, and 19.98 pp in Mozambique; Philippines changes little and Colombia rises 6.26 pp.

headline: Expansion beyond seven countries.
key_result: Requires comparable Planet roads, population, facilities, hazards, and computational pipeline for 30-50 additional countries.

headline: 2020 vs 2024 road-surface and access dynamics.
key_result: Large unpaved-to-paved shifts raise hazard resilience more than baseline access: Mozambique health hazard +6.05 pp; Pakistan health hazard +4.64 pp.

headline: Future flood/cyclone/precipitation projections.
key_result: Requires probabilistic future hazard footprints and exposure/protection assumptions.
